questions.question_text:
The table shows the mean and the range of the masses, in kilograms, of paper collected each week by two classes for a recycling drive.
$\begin{array}{lcc}\textbf{Class}&\textbf{Mean}&\textbf{Range}\\ \hline 8\text{B}&24&5\\ 8\text{F}&24&14\end{array}$
Which conclusion is best supported by the table?

options.text: The two classes collected the same amount per week on average, but $8$B was the more consistent.
$8$B collected more paper per week on average than $8$F.
options.why: Read the smaller range as a bigger total; the two means are both $24$ kg.

options.text: $8$F collected more paper per week on average, because its range is larger.
options.why: Treated the range as an amount collected rather than a measure of spread.

options.text: $8$F was the more consistent class, because its range is larger.
options.why: Reversed the rule: the smaller range, not the larger, means more consistent.

questions.solution_text:
$24 = 24$
The means are equal, so neither class collected more per week on average.
$5 < 14$
$8$B has the smaller range, so $8$B's weekly totals varied less.

questions.question_text:
The table shows summary information about two students' cricket scores last season.
$\begin{array}{lcc}\textbf{Student}&\textbf{Mean}&\textbf{Range}\\ \hline \text{Lena}&48&16\\ \text{Omar}&55&29\end{array}$
Which comparison is correct?

options.text: Omar scored more runs on average, but Lena was more consistent.
Omar scored more runs on average and was more consistent.
options.why: Correctly compared the means but treated the larger range of $29$ as greater consistency.

options.text: Lena scored more runs on average and was more consistent.
options.why: Correctly compared consistency but treated Lena's smaller mean of $48$ as more runs on average.

options.text: Lena scored more runs on average, but Omar was more consistent.
options.why: Reversed both comparisons: Omar has the higher mean, and Lena has the smaller range.

questions.solution_text:
$55 > 48$
Omar scored more runs on average.
$16 < 29$
Lena had the smaller range, so she was more consistent.

questions.question_text:
A school has $850$ students.
All $22$ members of its debating club are asked whether the school should hold a public-speaking day, and $19$ of them say yes.
A student concludes that most students at the school want a public-speaking day.
Why may this conclusion be invalid?

options.text: Debating club members may be more interested in public speaking than other students, who were not surveyed.
Asking every debating club member means the whole school was surveyed.
options.why: Confused covering the whole club with covering all $850$ students in the school.

options.text: Students outside the debating club must oppose a public-speaking day.
options.why: Treated students who were not asked as though they had answered no.

options.text: The conclusion must be valid because $19$ is more than half of $22$.
options.why: Used the majority within the selected club to justify a conclusion about the whole school without checking selection bias.

questions.solution_text:
The selected group consists only of debating club members.
They may have a stronger interest in public speaking than other students.
Students outside the club were not surveyed, so the club's responses may not represent the school's preferences.

questions.question_text:
A school put a second recycling bin in the playground at the start of Term $2$.
The mean mass of recycling collected each week rose from $31$ kg in Term $1$ to $44$ kg in Term $2$.
Which conclusion is best supported by this data?

options.text: More recycling was collected each week on average in Term $2$ than in Term $1$.
The extra bin caused the rise in the amount of recycling collected.
options.why: Assumed the one change noticed must be the cause; masses record what happened, not why.

options.text: Students cared more about the environment in Term $2$ than in Term $1$.
options.why: Concluded about attitudes, which the weekly masses never measured.

options.text: The mean mass collected each week will rise again in Term $3$.
options.why: Extended a past change into a term the data does not cover.

questions.solution_text:
$44 > 31$
The data records the mean mass collected each week in each term.
The means are all it measures, so the comparison of the two terms is the only conclusion it supports.

questions.question_text:
A school wants to investigate whether its $600$ students would buy a new canteen breakfast.
The first $40$ students in the canteen queue at recess are asked, and $31$ say yes.
Why may this sampling method give an unrepresentative sample?

options.text: Students in the canteen queue may be more interested in buying canteen food than other students, who were not surveyed.
Asking the first $40$ students in the queue guarantees that the sample represents the whole school.
options.why: Treated selection by queue order as a guarantee of representativeness, ignoring students outside the queue.

options.text: The sample must represent the school because $31$ is more than half of $40$.
options.why: Used the majority within the selected sample to judge representativeness instead of checking which students were included.

options.text: Every student outside the canteen queue would refuse to buy the new breakfast.
options.why: Assumed students who were not surveyed had answered no; their preferences are unknown.

questions.solution_text:
The sample includes only students already in the canteen queue at recess.
They may be more interested in buying canteen food than other students.
Students outside the queue were not surveyed, so the $31$ yes responses out of $40$ may not represent the preferences of all $600$ students.

questions.question_text:
The table shows summary information about the times, in seconds, taken by two groups to complete a shape puzzle.
$\begin{array}{lccc}\textbf{Group}&\textbf{Mean}&\textbf{Median}&\textbf{Range}\\ \hline \text{X}&27.6&27.2&9.8\\ \text{Y}&26.9&26.5&12.4\end{array}$
Which comparison is correct?

options.text: Group Y was faster on average, but Group X was more consistent.
Group X was faster on average and more consistent.
options.why: Correctly used the smaller range for consistency but treated a higher mean and median time as faster.

options.text: Group Y was faster on average and more consistent.
options.why: Correctly interpreted the lower mean and median times but treated the larger range as greater consistency.

options.text: Group X was faster on average, but Group Y was more consistent.
options.why: Reversed both rules: lower times mean faster completion, and a smaller range means greater consistency.

questions.solution_text:
$26.9 < 27.6$ and $26.5 < 27.2$
Group Y has the lower mean and median times, so it was faster on average.
$9.8 < 12.4$
Group X has the smaller range, so it was more consistent.
